pages.title: 6 Pieces for 3 Cellos, Op.104 (Dotzauer, Friedrich)
pages.reason: The cached page lists three separate cello parts and no recording; a professional human-performance floor was not established.
facts: Score/parts: cello 1, cello 2, cello 3; no human recording located.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists three distinct cello parts, six pieces, and a first-publication estimate of 1835; Performances shows no recordings.

pages.title: An Inness Sky (Fine, Elaine)
pages.reason: A complete score and parts are listed for three cellos, but the only cached audio is synthesized MIDI, which does not establish the required human-performance floor.
facts: Composition year 2006; listed duration 4 minutes; MIDI excluded as a performance floor.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists a complete score and parts for 3 cellos; its audio is labelled Synthesized Performance / Computer Generated.

pages.title: Sonata for 3 Violins in F major, ULB Mus.Ms.334 (Fux, Johann Joseph)
pages.reason: Original three-violin score materials and a commercial human recording of the exact ULB manuscript work were found; reconcile the page’s six-movement listing with the album’s four-track version before import.
facts: Original instrumentation is 3 violins; manuscript and edition score materials are available.
Commercial 2025 recording has four tracks totalling 9:28; cache lists six movements, so extent/version needs fact review.

sources.finding: IMSLP identifies ULB Mus.Ms.334 as a six-movement work for 3 violins and lists complete-score and complete-parts materials.
Presto lists a 2025 Azul Music/OSESP release of the exact ULB Mus.Ms.334 title, four movements, 9:28 total, performed by Emmanuele Baldini, Matthew Thorpe, and Anderson Farinelli.

pages.title: Suite for 4 Violins (Gabrielli, Ladislav)
pages.reason: The four-violin score is present, but the human audio is credited to “Steve’s Bedroom Band” without evidence of a professional performance/recording; MIDI does not upgrade the floor.
facts: Three movements; listed average duration 10 minutes; no professional performance floor verified.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists complete score and four violin parts; human audio credits “Steve’s Bedroom Band,” while the separate MIDI audio is synthesized.

pages.title: 6 Trios, Op.10 (Guignon, Jean-Pierre)
pages.reason: The original is open to several treble instruments and the only cached score file is for flute parts 1 and 3; do not infer a three-violin score from the category tag.
facts: No complete violin-specific score or human recording was established.

sources.finding: IMSLP describes the work for three flutes, recorders, violins, treble viols, or other treble instruments; the listed file is “Flutes 1 & 3 only.”

pages.title: 3 String Trios (Haydn, Joseph)
pages.reason: The page explicitly identifies these as arrangements from Haydn string-quartet movements, so they are not original works for three violins in this original-version batch.
facts: Page-level instrument listing alone is misleading; source identifies arrangement provenance.

sources.finding: IMSLP Extra Information says the three items are arrangements from Haydn String Quartet Op.1 movements; score files are transcribed for three violins.

pages.title: Divertimento for 3 Cellos in D major (Hofmann, Leopold)
pages.reason: Although the title says three cellos, the typeset full score is explicitly for two cellos and bass; keep the original instrument identity unresolved rather than converting bass to cello.
facts: Three movements; score labels show the third line as bass; no recording located.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists the fuller manuscript as parts and the typeset score as Cello 1, Cello 2, Cello 3/Bass; instrumentation says “3 cellos (or 2 cellos, bass).”

pages.title: 4 Pieces for 3 Violins, Op.104 (Hofmann, Richard)
pages.reason: Parts exist and a human recording is linked, but it is described as a student recital; professional performance floor not established.
facts: 3 violins; four movements; available performance evidence is amateur/student-level, not a professional floor.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists four movements, complete parts, and MP3 recordings credited to “Steve’s Bedroom Band.”
A YouTube upload describes only movement I at a 2018 Chloe Trevor Music Academy student recital.

pages.title: 2 Stücke, Op.5 (Klengel, Julius)
pages.reason: Four distinct cello parts and a commercially released complete performance of both pieces by the London Mozart Players provide a strong original-version lead.
facts: Four cellos, two pieces; commercial album recording, full work 8:50.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists four separate cello parts and identifies Serenade and Humoreske.
Presto lists both movements (8:50 total) on Cello Classics CC1007, performed by the London Mozart Players; its credits identify four cellists.

pages.title: Suite for 3 Cellos (Koessler, Hans)
pages.reason: The complete score and three distinct cello parts are present, but no professional human performance was found in the focused search.
facts: Five movements; no recording floor established.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists a complete score and cello 1–3 materials for the five-movement suite; no recording appears in the cached performance section.

pages.title: Tertsetti (Kuula, Toivo)
pages.reason: A complete score is listed alongside an earlier incomplete score, but no human recording or professionally performed floor was found.
facts: One movement; composition year listed as 1904; score completeness can be resolved from the complete version.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists a complete score and an earlier incomplete score missing the final 10-bar section; no recording is listed.

pages.title: Serenade for 4 Cellos, Op.29 (Lachner, Franz Paul)
pages.reason: Score materials for four cellos are available, but no human recording/performance floor was established.
facts: Composition date 1829; two movements; no performance floor found.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists complete parts and a typeset complete score for four cellos; no recording is listed.

pages.title: 3 Sonatinas, Op.90 (Lachner, Ignaz)
pages.reason: The page is a three-work set but only Sonatina No.3 has parts listed; no professional human performance was found, so individual-work extraction remains unverified.
facts: Three sonatinas; published 1880; only No.3 materials are currently listed.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists only Complete Parts for Sonatina No.3; it lists no scores and no recordings for the set.

pages.title: Double Bass Quartet (Lauber, Joseph)
pages.reason: The autograph score confirms four independent double-bass parts, and an ASU Faculty Artist recording exists, but the archive’s track list covers a partial set and labels its final item movement V; verify exact extent and quartet-level performer credits before treating it as a strong floor.
facts: Original instrumentation: 4 double basses; score is a manuscript complete score.
Human audio exists in a university recital archive, but completeness/performer attribution is unresolved.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists the 1942 autograph complete score for 4 double basses, in sounding pitch/solo tuning, and first publication by Yorke in 1975.
ASU Library archives a 2004 Faculty Artist Concert recording with Lauber tracks I, II, III and V; the indexed credits are event-wide and do not map performers to these tracks.
Yorke Edition identifies a four-movement work for double bass quartet, about 13 minutes, with several recordings and broadcasts.

pages.title: Cello Quartet, Op.11 (Limmer, Franz)
pages.reason: A complete four-part cello score is available, but no human recording/performance floor was established.
facts: Published 1830; four cellos; no performance floor located.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists complete parts for four cellos and four movements; its performance section has no recording.

pages.title: Nocturne for 4 Cellos, Op.90 (Maurer, Ludwig Wilhelm)
pages.reason: Four cello parts and an incipit are visible, but the score page provides no performance recording or professionally performed floor.
facts: First publication 1859 or earlier; no duration/movement count established.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists complete parts for four cellos and a four-staff incipit; no recording is listed.

pages.title: Suite for 3 Violins, Op.133 (Moór, Emanuel)
pages.reason: A complete score for three violins is available, but no human recording/performance floor was found.
facts: Four movements; no performance floor found.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists the complete score, four movements, 3 violins, and first publication in 1912; no recording is listed.

pages.title: Fortune (Rzewski, Frederic)
pages.reason: A complete score and named complete human performance by four violists are listed, but the available source does not establish a professional-performance/recording floor.
facts: One movement, composed 2005; recording exists but performer professionalism/production floor is unverified.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists a complete score for four violas (players also speaking) and a complete human performance credited to Leanne King, Dominic De Stefano, Michael Davis, and Sara Rogers.

pages.title: Andante religioso (Schmitt, Florent)
pages.reason: The page says this cello-quartet score is extracted from Schmitt’s Trombone Quartet Op.109; it is an arrangement of a different original instrumentation, not an original four-cello work.
facts: A complete score exists for the cello arrangement, but original work scoring is trombone quartet.

sources.finding: IMSLP explicitly says the cello-quartet and string-quartet/string-orchestra versions are extracted from the Trombone Quartet, Op.109.
Palazzetto Bru Zane concerts by four cellists were reported for the cello arrangement; that does not change the original work’s instrumentation.

pages.title: Concerto for 4 Violins, TWV 40:202 (Telemann, Georg Philipp)
pages.reason: The manuscript contains a complete set of four-violin parts, and Music@Menlo’s 2026 official page documents a professional performance by four named violinists with a paid livestream; resolve movement-count differences before import.
facts: Original work is for four violins; do not substitute the separate harpsichord-continuo edition.
Official performance floor exists; cached page movement count is three while other records describe four movements.

sources.finding: IMSLP lists a complete manuscript part set for four violins, plus a separate arranger-created edition with a continuo line; original work-info lists three sections.
Music@Menlo’s July 28, 2026 program lists this exact work and names Arnaud Sussmann, Stella Chen, Aaron Boyd, and Jessica Lee; the official page offered a livestream.
